app/app/routes.ts:5 — one route-config line to remove

app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:381 — Abilities section with the only /abilities links in the app

app/app/lib/data.server.ts:86 — SpeciesCard.hidden field is ability-only
removability.rationale: Deleting the route file is trivial, but the feature leaks a flag into the shared card type and component, so removal means small edits across five files instead of two.

evidence: app/app/lib/format.ts:5 — humanize, englishName, dexNumber, orDash all single-source; naming/format fixes land in one file
app/app/lib/data.server.ts:99 — sprite from species-ID pattern feeds ability/move/type cards
app/app/routes/home.tsx:90 — independent front_default sprite override; a sprite bug has two code paths to find
app/app/routes/ability.tsx:22 — card dedup/form-filter loop duplicates cardsFromRefs (data.server.ts:106)
app/app/lib/data.server.ts:117 and app/app/routes/ability.tsx:39 — by-dex sort implemented twice
changeability.rationale: Formatting and display-name rules are exemplary single-point changes, but card construction, sprite resolution and sort order each exist in two or three places, so those fixes land N times.

evidence: app/app/lib/data.server.ts:1 — all API knowledge isolated in a .server.ts module the bundler keeps out of the client
app/app/components/ui.tsx:60 — PokemonCard consumes a plain card object, not API payloads
app/app/routes/home.tsx:21 — loader typed ({ request }: any) instead of Route.LoaderArgs from ./+types
app/app/components/ui.tsx:63 — cards: any[] bypasses the existing SpeciesCard interface
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:142,292 — loader and component both any-typed; payload changes are not compiler-caught
coupling.rationale: Server/client split is clean and UI is decoupled from the API, but pervasive any typing erases the interface boundaries between loaders and components, which is where coupling bites during edits.

evidence: app/app/lib/data.server.ts:13 — cached() + getResource/getList/getByUrl stretch to any future resource (e.g. items) with no changes
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:70 — COLUMNS array drives the sortable table; adding a column is data, not code
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:31 — FIXED_METHODS + alphabetical fallback handles method-order variation declaratively
app/app/routes/type.tsx:16 — RELATIONS array declaratively maps the six damage-relation rows
app/app/routes/ability.tsx:22 — hidden-ability variation copy-pasted instead of parameterizing cardsFromRefs; SpeciesCard.hidden is a one-consumer flag (data.server.ts:86)
abstraction_design.rationale: The data/format/UI helpers genuinely stretch to similar cases and the tables are data-driven; the one real miss is the ability route duplicating the card pipeline rather than extending it.

findings.issue: Card-building loop (refId, id>10000 filter, dedup, sort) duplicates cardsFromRefs in app/app/lib/data.server.ts:106, differing only in the hidden flag — future card rules (sprite fix, new exclusion, sorting) must be applied in both.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardsFromRefs with an optional per-entry transform or a cardsFromAbility wrapper in data.server.ts so all card lists flow through one pipeline.

findings.issue: Every loader, meta and component is typed with any (home.tsx:21,110; pokemon.tsx:142,292; move.tsx:22; type.tsx:26; ability.tsx:15), discarding the framework's generated Route.LoaderArgs/ComponentProps types — changing a loader payload shape compiles cleanly and breaks silently.
findings.suggestion: Use `import type { Route } from "./+types/home"` and type loader args and component props, plus SpeciesCard for the card arrays (ui.tsx:63).

findings.issue: Card sprite resolution has two independent paths: the species-ID URL pattern here and the front_default override in app/app/routes/home.tsx:90; a sprite bug fix in one path leaves the other stale.
findings.suggestion: Resolve card sprites in one place (ideally in getSpeciesCardMap or a shared enrichCard helper) and have home consume it like the other lists.

findings.issue: Dex-number ordering of card lists is implemented here, in ability.tsx:39, and implicitly via the species index on home — a global order change (e.g., sort by name) needs three coordinated edits.
findings.suggestion: Centralize ordering in the card pipeline (or sort once inside PokemonCardList) so all four lists share it.

findings.issue: The { notFound: true } sentinel + meta guard + component guard pattern is repeated in four routes (move.tsx:27,36,55; type.tsx:31,51,60; pokemon.tsx:144,270,295; ability.tsx:20,37,45) instead of throwing a 404 Response handled by an ErrorBoundary.
findings.suggestion: Throw new Response(null, { status: 404 }) from loaders and render the 404 UI in the root ErrorBoundary (app/app/root.tsx:92); this also gives the encouraged real 404 status.

findings.issue: Identical meta functions are duplicated across four route modules; only the titleFor helper (app/app/lib/format.ts:37) is shared.
findings.suggestion: Minor, but a shared resourceMeta(title) helper in lib/format.ts would make title changes one-edit.

findings.issue: The loader is ~150 lines of inline data shaping (stats, abilities, evolution, games, move tables) in one function; nothing in it is extractable for an Items-shaped page that needs the same move-table shaping.
findings.suggestion: Extract move/version-group shaping into lib (e.g., buildMoveTables) so both Pokémon and future detail pages reuse it.

summary: This is a well-organized Framework Mode app: one server-only data module, one formatting module, and shared UI components mean most changes are findable and small, and the data-driven tables indicate good instincts. The editability risks are concrete and fixable: card construction, sprite resolution and card ordering are each duplicated in 2–3 places, and the pervasive any typing throws away the compiler help the framework's generated route types would give during exactly the kind of edits this app will need. I'd approve it after the card-pipeline dedup and typed loaders.
